reference.title: Scenario 2 — 2 — Column Table in API Reference Section

section.p: A section titled "POST /api/print-job" documents a REST API endpoint. The topic is classified as reference because the heading contains an API keyword and the body contains a 2-column parameter table.

table.title: Two-column table in API reference section

entry.codeblock:
POST /api/print-job

Submits a new print job to the queue.

Field Description
document_id ID of document to print.
copies Number of copies (default: 1).

<reference id="post_api_print_job"> <title>POST /api/print-job</title> <shortdesc>Submits a new print job to the queue.</shortdesc> <refbody> <properties frame="all" id="properties_z4h_mxg_pjc"> <prophead> <proptypehd>Field</proptypehd> <propvaluehd>Description</propvaluehd> </prophead> <property> <proptype>document_id</proptype> <propvalue>ID of document to print</propvalue> </property> <property> <proptype>copies</proptype> <propvalue>Number of copies (default: 1)</propvalue> </property> </properties> </refbody> </reference>

section.p: Result: The 2-column HTML <table> maps to <properties> because the topic is classified as API reference. The same table in a concept topic would produce <simpletable>.
section.note: A 2-column table maps to <properties>only when the topic is classified as reference with an API keyword context. Outside of that context, a 2-column HTML <table> always maps to <simpletable>.
section.p: For a complete summary of how HTML table structures map to DITA output elements, see Tables — Overview.
